subject: maths
question: Find the gain percentage, given that Priya sold her scooter for ₹42564 gaining (1)/(6)th of the selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since Gain is 1/6th of the Selling Price (SP), let us assume SP = 6 units.

This means Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 6 − 1 = 5 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹42564

Gain = 1/6 of Selling Price

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46da82e77e462f00237a9eb25103958cb51472f62b5bbbf3ab6dcdfd4171f5b0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Gain = (1 ÷ 6) × 42564 = ₹7094

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 42564 − 7094 = ₹35470

⇒ Gain % = (7094 ÷ 35470) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit & Loss Base Rule

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the question.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price is obtained as: SP = MP − (Discount % × MP ÷ 100).

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a trader sells goods at Cost Price but uses false weights, the profit percentage is given by: [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

A single equivalent discount for two successive discounts of a% and b% is given by the formula: (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.
